# Engine changelog

Every engine version, what it changed, and whether results stay comparable across it. Authored once in `scsim/CHANGELOG.yaml` and gated in CI (PLAN.md §25, gate `engine-ledger`). *Comparable* answers the user's question; *Tier* is the engineering classification (Part IX §9.5) — a patch can still change results for some projects.

## 0.6.1 · 2026-10-03 · Tier 2

**Changed for some projects.** Results change only for projects whose Supplier rows carry a typed s or S, a periodic review period, or an (R,Q) lot; every frozen reference run kept its digest.

A replenishment level typed on a /policies Supplier row is now exactly the level the run uses: no safety stock is added on top of it and it is never raised. Periodic review reads its review period per material, and an (R,Q) policy with a lot size orders up to R + Q.

*Technical.* P-P.1/P-P.3: a row's absolute s/S is the material's level (P-P.3 adds nothing on top at PH-70); periodic T read per material; (R,Q) with a lot has S = R + Q; Eq. 21 reads the row κ. Patch: no new phase or state key. Mapping warning text for `order_up_to` reworded.

- commit `53cf20cd`
- policies P-P.1, P-P.3
- KPIs `fill_rate`, `cost_of_resilience`, `delta_cost`
- frozen reference runs moved: none
- refs D288, WP 14.8

**Changed under this version without a bump:**

- 2026-10-03 · Tier 2 (`a603f6c4`) — (R,Q) has no κ: a κ stored on an (R,Q) row is no longer mapped, and a row with no positive Q keeps the declared fallback with a per-material warning.
- 2026-10-03 · Tier 2 (`e34945f4`) — A Supplier row's lead time (`lead_time_weeks`) is read as an override of its lane, for that link only, rounded and clamped as an upload is. Neutral for a project that sets none (D290).
- 2026-10-03 · Tier 1 — Build identity (WP 15.1): a run's code_version names its build by content (`scsim-0.6.1+<digest>` over scsim and the worker's compute path), the package version is ENGINE_VERSION (the wheel is scsim-0.6.1), and the version line no longer carries a comment. No result changes; every frozen reference run kept its digest.

*Written from git history by WP 15.4.*

## 0.6.0 · 2026-10-03 · Tier 3

**Comparable — results unchanged.** A new option: a project that does not select MRP runs byte-identically (frozen digests).

Materials can be planned by MRP: requirements are the bill of materials times planned production over the lead time, net of stock and what is already on the way, and at least the MOQ.

*Technical.* New transient key `gross_requirements` (PH-70); P-P.1 `policy_type = "mrp"`. The planning horizon H is the longest MRP lead time + 1. Pipeline schema re-frozen.

- commit `9492d9b2`
- ADR 0002
- policies P-P.1
- frozen reference runs moved: none
- refs D284, WP 14.5, ADR 0002

**Changed under this version without a bump:**

- 2026-10-03 · Tier 2 (`0c7ff8dd`) — `fulfillment_mode` is a Plant-row override of the product's mode (row → master → project → MTO); byte-identical for a project that sets none (D197, D283).
- 2026-10-03 · Tier 2 (`07449896`) — Demand is set only on the Customer stage: a Plant-row demand mean or CV override is no longer read, and the run log names one it ignores. A project that saved one simulates on its item-master / outbound demand from this build (D286).

## 0.5.0 · 2026-10-03 · Tier 3

**Changed for some projects.** Results change for make-to-stock projects that set a finished-goods policy or opening stock, or that typed an S beside P-P.4; every frozen reference run kept its digest.

Production is planned over a horizon as the smaller of the requirement and capacity. Finished goods can follow a base-stock, min-max or days-of-cover policy, with opening stock.

*Technical.* New transient key `planned_production` (PH-40). FG policies base-stock / min-max / days of cover and FG opening stock; P-P.4 never adds on top of a typed S. Pipeline schema re-frozen.

## 0.4.0 · 2026-10-03 · Tier 3

**Changed for some projects.** Results change for projects allocating by `revenue_max` or `sla_tier`, or that set per-row backorder; every frozen reference run kept its digest.

Each customer × product row is fulfilled on its own: its own backlog, backorder window, priority and service-level target.

*Technical.* P-C.1 reads `demand_rows` (a hook-contract change). `revenue_max` allocation is real (was priority); a customer's `sla_fill_floor_pct` is its rows' default target under sla_tier; max backorder days round half up.

## 0.3.0 · 2026-10-02 · Tier 3

**Changed for some projects.** Results change for every project with a `normal` demand distribution (a different distribution, not only different draws) and for projects that set row demand.

Demand is drawn per customer × product row, from a forecast series or from a mean, a variation and a distribution. A `normal` demand is now a real normal distribution.

*Technical.* New transient key `demand_rows` (PH-10) with its own consumption contract; product demand is the row sum. `DemandModel.NORMAL` is N(μ, cv·μ), clipped at 0, clips reported (it ran as triangularAV). Pipeline schema re-frozen.

- commit `019222b9`
- ADR 0002
- policies P-C.4
- KPIs `fill_rate`, `lost_sales_value`, `delta_cost`
- frozen reference runs moved: none
- refs D284, WP 14.1, ADR 0002

## 0.2.7 · 2026-09-22 · Tier 2

**Changed for some projects.** Results can change for runs with automatic warm-up, where the adopted warm-up week moves; rare and small in the reference set.

Automatic warm-up detection uses the published MSER-5 statistic (White, 1997).

*Technical.* mser5 is z(d) = Σ(b−b̄)²/(n_b−d)². The old statistic is reported for one release as `WarmupReport.mser5_legacy_week` and adopted by nothing. Of 36 auto-warm-up reference scenarios the adopted warm-up changed in 1 (week 50 → 60); its fill rate moved +0.0003, inside its CI.

- commit `950d07f0`
- KPIs `fill_rate`, `lost_sales_value`, `delta_cost`
- frozen reference runs: predates them
- refs audit F-25

*Written from git history by WP 15.4. 1 further engine-source commit(s) under this version are described by no record.*

## 0.2.6 · 2026-09-22 · Tier 2

**Changed for some projects.** Projects with stochastic lead times get different draws from the same distribution: same expected results, different individual replications.

Random lead times are drawn per link and week up front, so two policies compared on the same seed see the same lead times.

*Technical.* F-24: stochastic lead-time variates pre-drawn per (link, week) from the world stream (CRN across policies); `StatisticsReport.stopping_rule` recorded.

- commit `5e8b9b86`
- KPIs `fill_rate`, `cost_of_resilience`, `delta_cost`
- frozen reference runs: predates them
- refs audit F-13, audit F-24

## 0.2.5 · 2026-09-22 · Tier 2

**Changed for some projects.** Fill rate changes only for runs that had analysis windows with no demand.

A window with no demand has no fill rate (it was reported as 100 %), and averages exclude replications where a KPI could not be measured.

*Technical.* F-08: window FR is NaN → null with no demand (weekly FR keeps 1.0 for a no-demand week); `aggregate_mean_ci` excludes unmeasured replications; an all-NaN KPI aggregates to NaN.

## 0.2.4 · 2026-09-22 · Tier 2

**Changed for some projects.** Recovery KPIs change for runs with censored recovery or with a disruption starting inside the warm-up.

Recovery times are never substituted: a censored time-to-recover is a flag, not a number, and a fixed disruption start inside the warm-up moves to its end and is reported.

*Technical.* F-03: a fixed start before t_w shifts to t_w and is counted (`event_shifts`). F-04: no substituted TTR baseline. F-05: `ttr_censored` / `tts_censored` flags.
